chunks: That which the Sheikh — may God the Most High support him — informed me of: he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub and Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
«There is no wudu (required) for kissing, nor for direct bodily contact, nor for touching the private parts.»

key_terms.الْقُبْلَةِ: kissing — a marital act not classified as a ritual nullifier of wudu in Shia fiqh
key_terms.الْمُبَاشَرَةِ: direct bodily/skin-to-skin contact short of intercourse — likewise not a wudu nullifier
key_terms.مَسِّ الْفَرْجِ: touching the private parts — a wudu nullifier according to Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, but not in Shia law
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu — the ritual ablution required before salat, invalidated only by specific acts defined in Shia fiqh

ai.seo_question: Does kissing or touching the private parts invalidate wudu according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) rules that kissing, mubashara (direct skin-to-skin contact), and touching the private parts do not necessitate wudu. This is a foundational Shia jurisprudential position that distinguishes Imami fiqh from the Shafi'i and Hanbali schools, which hold that touching the private parts — or in some opinions touching a woman — invalidates wudu. The ruling appears in the chapter on acts that do necessitate taharah, serving as a clarifying counter-position.
